subject.title: [Feature]: Standardize skill data directory convention (configPaths) under ~/.openclaw/

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class per-skill writable data contract, and if so should it be a filesystem convention, plugin/skill data API, or ClawHub authoring rule?
rationale: The code lacks the requested contract, but adding one creates durable storage, metadata, and compatibility behavior that should be chosen intentionally before an automated fix PR changes skill semantics.

options.title: Design a core skill-data contract
options.body: Sponsor a narrow API or metadata convention and require docs, installer behavior, and migration expectations to land together.

options.title: Publish ClawHub authoring guidance only
options.body: Keep runtime unchanged and tell skill authors to follow a registry/documented path convention without core enforcement.

options.title: Reject a new data surface for now
options.body: Leave skill data fully skill-owned until stronger user demand or a concrete missing plugin API proves the need.

recommendation.title: Design a core skill-data contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a narrow API or metadata convention and require docs, installer behavior, and migration expectations to land together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent skill lifecycle/runtime history and docs work make this the best available owner for the product/storage-boundary choice.
